purpose: Public-program eligibility evidence only. No account-specific entitlement is claimed and no resource creation is authorized.

observed_public_limits.ampere_a1_monthly_free_allowance: 1500 OCPU-hours and 9000 GB-hours; current Always Free documentation equates this to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB RAM total

material_risks: Oracle documents that idle Always Free compute instances may be reclaimed when CPU and network utilization remain below 20% over a 7-day period; A1 also applies a memory-utilization threshold.
Always Free compute capacity can be temporarily unavailable in the home region.
Account home region, remaining Always Free quotas, current shape capacity, and billing state are not observable from public documentation.
BE-06 does not accept synthetic load generation as a persistence strategy; reclaim/recovery must be resolved by real operational evidence.
promotion_blockers: zero-cost resource selection not yet machine-checked

reclaim_disposition.acceptance_rule: A real right-sized A1 workload must be observed not to satisfy Oracle's documented idle-reclamation conditions; otherwise Oracle is rejected as the persistent host.

cost_estimate_semantics.official_estimator_limitation: Oracle documentation states that Console cost estimates are based on the organization's rate card and do not include tier unit pricing when applicable.

observed_public_limits.compute: one non-preemptible e2-micro VM per month within the eligible-hour allowance

external_ip_pricing.ipv4: Static and ephemeral external IPv4 addresses assigned to VMs are billed under current VPC pricing.
external_ip_pricing.ipv6: External IPv6 addresses assigned to VM instances are documented as no-charge.
external_ip_pricing.zero_cost_implication: A straightforward public IPv4 origin violates BE-06's 0 USD ceiling. An IPv6-only origin would require separate reachability and TLS acceptance evidence.

material_risks: The Free Tier e2-micro VM has a 1 GB memory envelope, so real node + gateway + TLS runtime headroom must still be reproduced.
Current Google VPC pricing charges static and ephemeral external IPv4 addresses assigned to VMs; this violates the BE-06 0 USD ceiling for the straightforward IPv4 design.
External IPv6 assigned to VMs is documented as no-charge, but IPv6-only public reachability across Explorer users and exact HTTPS/IP-certificate automation are not yet accepted.
The Free Tier includes only 1 GB/month outbound data transfer from North America to most destinations; public Explorer traffic must remain fail-closed before overage.
Billing-account state, free-tier consumption, quota, and regional VM availability are not observable from public documentation.
promotion_blockers: zero-cost broadly reachable public HTTPS path unresolved because external IPv4 is billed
1 GB RAM sufficiency not yet reproduced on a real constrained host
egress overage guard not yet proven
zero-cost resource selection not yet machine-checked

decision.reason: Oracle Cloud returns to first probe because Always Free offers a public-IP-capable persistent VM envelope with substantially more compute/storage/egress headroom at 0 USD, while Google charges VM external IPv4 addresses. Oracle still must pass a real idle-reclamation guard without synthetic load. Google remains fallback via a separately proven IPv6-only zero-cost path or later bounded paid authority.
